findings.title: Both allowlists admit any flag after `ls-remote --heads <remote>`, including `--upload-pack=<cmd>`
findings.recommendation: The spec row is `ls-remote --heads <resolved-remote> <ref>…`: refs only. Refuse every dash-prefixed argument after the remote in gitAllowed (run.ts) and in the transcribed allowedGit (instrument.ts), and add `ls-remote --heads origin --upload-pack=<cmd>` to the injected-write cases. The walk closed symbolic-ref and diff; this is the sibling the same closure misses.
findings.reproduction: node --input-type=module -e "import { gitAllowed } from './dist/core/pr/run.js'; console.log(gitAllowed(['ls-remote','--heads','origin','--upload-pack=touch /tmp/x'], 'origin'))" prints true (expected false: the row admits refs only); instrument.ts's allowedGit tests only rest[0] === '--heads' and rest.length >= 3, so it accepts the same argv.

findings.title: `git status --porcelain` refreshes `.git/index` as a side effect, an unnamed write inside an observe-only command
findings.recommendation: Set GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 in the runner's spawn environment beside GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, which git documents as preventing status from refreshing the index; or name the stat-cache refresh in the requirement's BOUNDED residual beside the fetch's side effects.
findings.reproduction: In a scratch repo: commit a file, touch it, read .git/index's mtime, sleep 1, run git status --porcelain, read the mtime again: 1791769836 then 1791769837 — the index was rewritten.

commentary: Graded every resolved entry over its sweep scope: the walk's src diff since 0536cf56, the delta, design and proposal edits, the generated surface (no 'never shells' left in .claude/), and the new cases, each of which the walk had shown to fail on the pre-walk code. The residual check found no file outside the entries' edit records. Both findings sit beside F2's closure rather than in it: having closed symbolic-ref and diff by reading their flags, I probed the remaining rows the same way — ls-remote takes arbitrary trailing flags, and status, though named in the row, writes the index's stat cache unless optional locks are off.
